estimates.t: For a description of our policies regarding our critical accounting estimates, see “Critical Accounting Estimates” in Part II , Item 7 “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” included in our 2025 10-K.

statements.t: The Company remains on track to continue to reduce net debt leverage ratio (3) toward 3.0x by the end of FY 2026 and below 3.0x during 1H FY 2027 (8) .
At G2E, we showcased our robust product and content roadmap, which is expected to drive momentum in the fourth quarter of 2026 and beyond.
Gaming machine sales totaled 8,906 new units shipped globally in the quarter, at the high end of our prior guidance range, including more than 5,800 new units in North America.

To maximize both customer and shareholder value, we expect to leverage this momentum while staying focused on disciplined execution that drives strong cash flows and allows us to both reinvest in product innovation and talent and further reduce leverage to deliver on our commitment.”

As signaled last quarter, we prioritized deleveraging over share repurchases, reducing our net debt leverage ratio (2) by approximately 0.1x sequentially, keeping us on track to fall below 3.0x during the first half of 2027 (4) .
We remain committed to prioritizing this deleveraging path in the fourth quarter and beyond, as we continue progressing toward our long-term financial targets (4) .”

• Principal face value of debt outstanding (1) was $5.0 billion , translating to a net debt leverage ratio (2) of 3.3x as of September 30, 2026, representing a 0.1x reduction from June 30, 2026 (3.4x), as we remain committed and on track to reduce our net debt leverage ratio (2) to below 3.0x during the first half of 2027 (3) .

• FY 2026 financial outlook: Full-year Consolidated AEBITDA (2) growth is expected to be toward the lower end of our previously announced range of mid-to-high single digits (3) , with Adjusted NPATA (2) growing faster than Consolidated AEBITDA (3) , and EPSa (2) growing faster than Adjusted NPATA (3) as we benefit from previous share buy-back activities.

The outlook reflects weakness in the social casino market and some delayed timing of investments and capital expenditures of our customer base, partially offset by our growing recurring revenue (5) base and an expected seasonally strong fourth quarter.
• the possibility that the Company may be unable to achieve expected financial, operational and strategic benefits of the Grover acquisition;
